composing_text: SS-Panzer Regiment 9; SS-Panzergrenadier Regiments 19 and 20; SS-Panzer Artillery Regiment 9; SS-Reconnaissance Battalion 9; SS-Anti-Tank Battalion 9; SS-Anti-Aircraft Battalion 9; SS-Panzer Pioneer Battalion 9
notes: Counter-attacked with 10th SS in the afternoon of 29 June (Cheux/Hill 112 area); 19th and 20th Regiments renewed attacks on Grainville-sur-Odon and Le Valtru at night 29-30 June without success. Brought back to France during June (CMH).

notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 9. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Bereits am 11. Juli kam es zu schweren Kämpfen bei Maltot und Eterville"; Wikipedia gives 10-11 July for Operation Jupiter, the British VIII Corps attack on Hill 112 and Maltot. Location: Maltot, the first of the two villages named; the point is the village, with a precision of 3 km. Location support: moderate: the Lexikon names both villages; the Wikipedia article gives the operation dates only. Context: the Lexikon adds that in mid-July one battalion of each SS Panzer Grenadier regiment had to be dissolved after the losses.

current_activity: Model directs the Fifth Panzer Army to release the 9th SS Panzer Division to the vicinity of Arnhem for rehabilitation
notes: Event date: CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 6 p. 127: "On 3 September the Army Group B commander had directed that the Fifth Panzer Army, retreating in disorder from France, release the 9th and 10th SS Panzer Divisions to move to the vicinity of Arnhem for rehabilitation". Event definition: the order of 3 September; the division did not arrive that day. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Arnhem with a precision of 25 km, the vicinity named by the order. Location approximate: the destination of the order, not a documented position. Location support: CMH names the vicinity. Commander: unknown.
